# Empirical Evaluation and Clinical Validation



## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the seven benchmarked architectures defined in Chapter 2 across 12 multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across 3 independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, 756 train/test fits), plus 189 paired reruns with non-negative loadings on the three high-dimensional cohorts and a 1,025-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, one seed). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features from the ANTsPyT1w/ANTsPyMM pipelines: the volumes of 160 hierarchical segmentation labels (View 0: cortical, subcortical, ventricular, white-matter and cerebellar labels), the volume-to-surface-area ratio of the same 160 labels (View 1; for a cortical label it tracks thickness, otherwise it is a shape index), and DiReCT cortical thickness averaged in each of 62 Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) cortical regions (View 2) [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N =$ 822) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Against Single-Matrix Factorization**: The leading mean Friedman ranks on the linear entrypoint probe are `NED` (3.00), `NEDPP` (3.33), `Flow-SiMR-V` (3.58), `LEND` (3.58), against `PCA` (5.38) and `NSAFlow-PCA` (5.42) (@fig-benchmark-uncertainty). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` reaches a linear score of 0.727 (`mfeat` accuracy) and 0.291 (`Shared+Private` $R^2$), against 0.973 (`NED`) and 0.949 (`SiMLR`) for the best multi-view model. Over the 12 datasets (seeds averaged, Wilcoxon signed-rank against `PCA` with Holm adjustment, @sec-app-operational), the linear score differs from `PCA` at $p < 0.05$ for 0 of 6 non-PCA models.
2. **Coordinate Alignment and the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct mechanisms across columns. With coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` loses -0.044 on average across the 12 cohorts (Random Forest minus linear score), falling from 0.125 to -0.000 on the weak sparse factors of `NonnegPartsWeak` and from 0.148 to 0.042 on `ADNI-MCI` (72% lower). The smallest drops are `SiMLR` (-0.017), `NEDPP` (-0.020).
3. **Operating Points and Feature Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support shows the quantile threshold $q$ as a lens on feature support recovery without conflating scales on secondary axes. Across the 756 default-positivity fits, the mean linear score is 0.713, 0.716 and 0.715 at $q = \text{None}$, $0.5$ and $0.8$, and the mean Random Forest axis score is 0.687, 0.689 and 0.688; at $q = 0.8$, 57.8% of loadings are zero while 99.8% of the best linear score is retained. At $q = 0.5$, support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ 0.500 (`PCA`) to 1.000 (`NSAFlow-PCA`), and reaches 0.875 on `NonnegParts` (`Flow-SiMR-V`). On the focal $20\%$-active modules, the best $F_1$ at $q = 0.8$ is 0.831 on `NonnegPartsWeak` (`Flow-SiMR-V`) and 0.660 on `Shared+Private` (`Flow-SiMR-V`).

## Non-Subtractive Sparsification and Two-Stage Uniform Shrinkage: Synthetic Verification (Propositions 1–3) {#sec-exp-synthetic-v043}

Numerical checks and 20-seed synthetic benchmarks verify Propositions 1–3 and two-stage support-restricted uniform shrinkage (`results_cache/v043_synthetic_theorems.json` from `scripts/benchmark_synthetic_theorems.py`; @sec-non-subtractive-sparsification; @sec-uniform-shrinkage; @donoho1994ideal).



1. **Proposition 1 (Subtractive Shrinkage Cancellation, @eq-prop1-cancellation):** Across shrinkage levels $\alpha \in [0, 0.99]$ on $p = 100$ coordinates at $q = 0.30$, order-statistic quantile soft-thresholding (`sparseness_alg="soft"`) yields maximum $\ell_\infty$ deviation $1.07 \times 10^{-15}$ from the $\alpha = 0$ support and weights, confirming exact $\alpha$-cancellation. Under uniform-shrunk coordinate floors, continuous pre-retraction soft-thresholding (`sparseness_type="soft"`, `_apply_soft_threshold_sparseness`) suffers floor erosion: at $\alpha = 0.99$, the uniform floor reaches 0.0826 above the threshold $\tau =$ 0.0415, pulling cosine similarity with $\alpha = 0$ down to 0.666 (@fig-v043-propositions A).
2. **Proposition 2 (Exact Top-$m$ Cardinality and Radial Simplex Normalization, @eq-prop2-radial-simplex):** On $p = 60, m = 20$, exact cardinality-constrained projection preserves the Cauchy–Schwarz variance bound with absolute error $0.00 \times 10^{0}$ and achieves lower Euclidean squared error (68.53 vs. 69.24) and higher cosine similarity (0.894 vs. 0.855) than shifted soft-thresholding. At `sparseness=None` ($p = 100$), legacy Euclidean simplex projection subtracts $\theta =$ 0.1285, zeros 81% of active coordinates, and lowers cosine similarity with the input direction to 0.718, whereas radial simplex normalization retains cosine 1.000 with zero dropped coordinates (@fig-v043-propositions B).
3. **Proposition 3 (Column-Support Uniform Shrinkage Orthogonality, @eq-prop3-support-shrinkage):** On $k = 2$ disjoint column supports of size [40, 40], `ColumnSupportShrinkageOperator` maintains exact orthogonality across $\alpha \in [0, 1]$ with maximum Gram Frobenius error $9.99 \times 10^{-16}$, whereas global `UniformShrinkageOperator` mixes the supports until Frobenius error reaches 1.414 and column cosine reaches 1.000 at $\alpha = 1$ (@fig-v043-propositions C).

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 =$ 0.148 $\pm$ 0.010 of out-of-sample cognitive variance (`CogPC1`) on the linear probe and 0.042 on the single-axis Random Forest probe. Aligning the MRI projections with the 11-scale cognitive battery during training gives, for the four leading models (3-seed means $\pm$ SD), `NED` (0.209 $\pm$ 0.027), `Flow-SiMR-V` (0.198 $\pm$ 0.021), `NEDPP` (0.192 $\pm$ 0.022), `LEND` (0.192 $\pm$ 0.029); the best is +41.2% over `PCA`. The best single-axis Random Forest score is 0.155 (`Flow-SiMR-V`), 3.7 times that of `PCA`. In the single-seed sweep the best configuration reaches 0.2686 (`Flow-SiMR-V`) and the best linear-family configuration 0.2595 (`SiMLR`), against 0.1869 for `PCA`; mean prediction across all eleven scales reaches 0.124 (`Flow-SiMR-V`) against 0.085 for `PCA` (+46.0%). These sweep peaks are maxima over many configurations on one split and are optimistic.
2. **Which MRI Features Carry the Prediction**: @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship attributes the held-out `CogPC1` prediction of the non-negative $q = 0.85$ fit (all nine MRI columns, $R^2 =$ 0.170). One column per MRI view carries it. Alone, the predictive column gives $R^2 =$ 0.122 in volume (component 1), 0.195 in vol/area (component 1) and 0.084 in DiReCT thickness (component 2, 1 region), against at most 0.068 for any other column, and only the vol/area column is not redundant with the rest (unique $R^2$ +0.040). Component numbers are not identifiable across fits, so the refits below follow each view's predictive column rather than a fixed index. Across 20 half-sample refits, the predictive vol/area basis selects these features in at least half of them (fraction of refits): L entorhinal (DKT parcellation): 0.95; L temporal lobe: 0.90; L inferior parietal (DKT cortex label): 0.85; L entorhinal (DKT cortex label): 0.80; R entorhinal (DKT cortex label): 0.80; R entorhinal (DKT parcellation): 0.75. These are mostly entorhinal, temporal-lobe and inferior parietal measures, the regions where atrophy is expected in prodromal Alzheimer's disease [@dickerson2009cortical; @jack2018nia]. DiReCT thickness tells the same story less clearly. Its first principal component explains 58% of the variance across the 62 regions (mean inter-region correlation 0.55), and consensus component 1 correlates 0.87 with subject-mean thickness, so hard-assigning each region to its largest structure coefficient places 62 / 0 / 0 regions on components 1 / 2 / 3: a display of the global factor, not of localisation (Panel B). The thickness basis itself is unstable under the default collapse penalty: it keeps two or fewer regions in 8 of 20 refits (median held-out $R^2$ 0.118). Non-negative region sums on positively correlated features typically correlate above the penalty's threshold of 0.3, so the penalty pushes those columns towards one or two regions. With `collapse_weight = 0` the predictive thickness basis keeps a median of 9 regions (two or fewer in 1 refit), its median $R^2$ rises to 0.144, and its most frequent regions are (fraction of refits) L entorhinal: 0.55; L supramarginal: 0.45 (Panel D). No single thickness region replicates in more than 0.55 of refits, so the thickness map is a pattern, not a list of identified regions (`docs/audit/evidence/adni_global_factor_check.csv`). For reference, unthresholded non-negative fits are 67% sparse on the DKT view without rotation and 67% with Varimax, against 0% for dense `PCA`.

Under `positivity="conical"`, 48 of 48 fits converge with maximum Gram defect $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \le$ $3.79 \times 10^{-14}$ and maximum inter-column cosine 0.000. Under radial simplex `positivity="convex"`, 45 of 48 fits converge with maximum inter-column cosine 0.000 and maximum Gram defect 0.482 (non-zero defect arises because radial $\ell_1$-simplex columns have unequal $\ell_2$ norms when disjoint support sizes differ). The three non-converged `convex` fits are all on `Diabetes` ($p = [5, 5]$) at $k = 2$ (`Stop_Reason = "no_descent"` across seeds `42, 43, 44`, consensus 0.273, linear 0.353), whereas `positivity="conical"` converges in all $3/3$ splits with consensus 0.331, linear 0.405, and Gram defect $1.78 \times 10^{-15}$. Pooled across cohorts for `conical`, mean consensus score rises from 0.463 ($k = 1$, linear 0.524) to 0.530 ($k = 2$, linear 0.641) and 0.572 ($k = 3$, linear 0.681). At each cohort's target rank ($k = 2$ for `Heart` and `Diabetes`, $k = 3$ for `ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics`, `TCGA-KIRC`, and `mfeat`), `fit_uniform_shrunk` (`conical`) reaches linear scores of 0.925 (`MultiOmics`), 0.931 (`mfeat`), 0.830 (`Heart`), 0.662 (`TCGA-KIRC`), 0.405 (`Diabetes`), and 0.209 (`ADNI-MCI`).
